business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Consignment and Secondhand Luxury Goods Retail

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: constitutional parliamentary monarchy rooted in common law; Alberta is a common-law province, with federal and provincial statutory regimes operating under the Constitution Act, 1867.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-EU Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA, entered into force 2014)
Applicable Canada Double Taxation Avoidance Conventions (DTAAs) with the residence jurisdictions of the ultimate beneficial owners

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part XII.2; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (5th Supp.); Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, as amended with respect to beneficial ownership transparency; Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9; Alberta Business Names Registration Act and Regulation; FINTRAC CDD/UBO enforcement guidance and Canada Revenue Agency administrative practice.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certification of each UBO/director's passport and proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in UBO's home country; passport issuing state for underlying identity document

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Certificate of Good Standing / Corporate Status certificate for any non-resident corporate shareholder or ULC member
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original jurisdiction's corporate registry or companies office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization depending on source state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth statement for each beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution and notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney and ULC subscription/incorporator consent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the jurisdiction where the incorporator or authorized agent signs

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence before incorporation. All directors, shareholders, ULC members and ultimate beneficial owners must be screened against PEP databases, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, EU/UK consolidated financial sanctions, the Canadian consolidated autonomous sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act, FINTRAC reporting thresholds, and domestic law-enforcement/watchlist indicators. For a Medium_Risk_Enhanced online consignment luxury resale entity, source of wealth, source of funds, expected turnover, and every payment rail counterparty must be verified, with independent documentation retained for anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing compliance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (official government portal: www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry; name search uses the Canada-wide NUANS Name Search System through authorized Alberta registry service providers)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be registered in English or French, or a combination, with the legal element 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' as required for an Alberta unlimited liability corporation. A non-Latin-script name must be transliterated into the Roman alphabet and supported by a sworn translation or statutory declaration explaining its meaning and pronunciation; accents and diacritical marks are preserved in Unicode only where the resulting name is not confusingly similar to an existing corporate name or trade name in Alberta.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A valid NUANS report is current for 90 days; the applicant may, before expiry, request an extension through an authorized Alberta registry agent. If the Registrar rejects the proposed name as prohibited or confusingly similar, the applicant may file a written Request for Name Reconsideration with Service Alberta/Corporate Registry within 30 calendar days, supplying a fresh NUANS report, consent letters from any affected regulated bodies, evidence of trade-mark search, and a statutory declaration of distinctiveness. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may apply for judicial review in the Alberta Court of King's Bench within the limitation period prescribed by the Alberta Rules of Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. The ABCA requires a registered office in Alberta at a physical street address capable of receiving legal service of process. For an online consignment and secondhand luxury-goods e-commerce ULC, a commercial virtual-office or registered-agent suite is acceptable provided it is an actual Alberta street address, the provider accepts service of process on behalf of the corporation, corporate records are accessible, and the arrangement is not a post-office-box-only facility.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated annual probability below 5% for an unannounced on-site inspection of a non-licensed online resale e-commerce business. Provincial registries and the CRA are predominantly document-driven; physical inspections are unlikely except in response to suspected counterfeit luxury goods, trade-mark infringement, unreported cash deliveries, or FINTRAC/AML substantive-examination triggers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9 (Alberta), ss. 5-10 (incorporation and Articles of Incorporation), s. 15.1 (Unlimited Liability Corporation regime), ss. 101-105 (registered office and director requirements), ss. 123-124 (by-laws and share subscription); supplemental registration under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act and CRA Excise Tax Act (GST/HST).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta – Corporate Access online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form INC-1) filed with the Registrar of Corporations, culminating in the issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Alberta Business Corporations Act; the ULC may incorporate with nominal authorized share capital (e.g., an unlimited number of no-par-value Common Shares). No escrow account or capital deposit is required at incorporation, and non-resident shareholding is permitted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Corporation adopts the Articles of Incorporation as filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry, and the share subscription of the initial Shareholders is ratified; that the registered office of the Corporation shall be situated at [address], City of [X], Province of Alberta, and [Name] is appointed as the registered agent; that [Name] is elected President, [Name] Secretary and [Name] Treasurer of the Corporation until successors are appointed. FURTHER RESOLVED that the corporate seal and the form of share certificate be approved, and that the officers are authorized to open banking accounts, register the Corporation for taxation, obtain all business licences, and execute all documents required to commence the Corporation's operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Corporate Name Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – Corporate Access (Service Alberta, Government of Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a discretionary name search request in the Corporate Access portal for the proposed corporate name, e.g., '[Name] ULC,' and obtain a NUANS (Newly Updated Automated Name Search) report. Verify that the name is distinguishable from existing corporate identifiers and trademarks and does not contain prohibited terms. Pay the CAD 20 search fee online. The reservation remains valid for 90 calendar days, within which the Articles of Incorporation must be filed.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report (printed and retained)
Proposed corporate name incorporating the legal element 'ULC'
Written authorization from any third party whose name is included in the proposed name, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on confusion or prohibited-terms grounds, re-file the NUANS request with a new name or an added distinguishing element, attach consent letters from any conflicting name holder, or request a review by the Registrar within 30 days of the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Electronic Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – Corporate Access electronic filing system (Service Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form INC-1 (Articles of Incorporation) using the prescribed statutory template. State expressly that the Corporation is an Unlimited Liability Corporation; include the authorized share structure (e.g., an unlimited number of Common Shares with no par value), the registered office address in Alberta, and the names and addresses of the first directors. Execute the Articles, obtain director consents, and submit through Corporate Access with the CAD 150 incorporation fee. The Registrar reviews the record for statutory completeness.
required_dossiers: Form INC-1 Articles of Incorporation (executed PDF)
Valid NUANS name search report
Consent of First Directors (Form 1)
Registered Office Information Form
Payment of CAD 150 incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a technical defect or deficiency notice, file a written correction and amended record within 30 days, resubmitting the electronic filing; a new NUANS report and re-filing fee apply only if the corporate name is changed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Organizational Board Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (certificate issuance) and the Board of Directors of the Corporation (organizational governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration of the Articles, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation. Convene an organizational meeting of the first director(s) to: (i) fix the registered office address and confirm the registered agent; (ii) adopt By-law No. 1; (iii) ratify the share subscription and issue shares to the initial Shareholders; (iv) appoint the President, Secretary and Treasurer; and (v) approve the corporate banking resolution. Record all proceedings in written minutes executed by the corporate secretary.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Notice of Registered Office
Draft By-law No. 1
Share subscription agreement and share certificate book
Minutes of the First Board Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed by-laws or share issuance conflict with the Alberta Business Corporations Act or the ULC designation, re-draft the affected instruments, circulate revised resolutions, re-execute the minutes, and record any director dissent in the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online) and Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (Provincial Tax Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Corporation with the CRA through Business Registration Online to obtain a Business Number (BN), a corporate income tax program account, and a GST/HST program account if annual worldwide taxable revenues exceed the CAD 30,000 threshold. Register the corporation with the Alberta Corporate Tax system within 90 days of incorporation, confirming the fiscal year-end and registered office address. The ULC should also document its pass-through eligibility for U.S. federal tax check-the-box purposes in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Alberta registered office address and director information
Fiscal year-end confirmation
Estimated annual revenue for GST/HST threshold determination
ULC classification memorandum for U.S. check-the-box election
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA queries the application, respond to the written notice within 30 days with the missing corporate documents and request back-dating of the Business Number to the date of incorporation; for Alberta, file a voluntary correction in the Provincial Tax Portal and maintain correspondence in the tax compliance file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Secondhand Goods Dealer Permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Business Licensing Department of the city where the registered office is situated (e.g., City of Calgary Business Licensing, Business Licence Bylaw 6M96)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a business licence application for an online consignment and secondhand luxury goods resale operation. Because the Corporation buys and sells used goods, obtain a Second-Hand Goods Dealer Licence: disclose the premises address, principal place of business, directors, and online operating model; provide a police background clearance for the licence applicant; and remit the applicable municipal fee. Maintain a daily acquisition-and-disposition register for all secondhand goods acquired or sold, renew the licence annually, and keep the licence displayed at the licensed premises.
required_dossiers: Municipal business licence application (retail/trade category)
Second-Hand Goods Dealer licence application form
Police background check for the licence applicant
Certificate of Incorporation and CRA Business Number
Proof of premises occupancy (lease or title)
Proposed secondhand goods acquisition and disposition register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence is refused, request a written reconsideration or hearing before the municipal Licence Appeal Committee, submit supplementary authenticity-control and source-verification policies for luxury goods, and, where the bylaw permits, apply for an interim operating authorization pending disposition of the appeal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental, Fire Safety and Occupational Health Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas; municipal fire marshal; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (Labour, Immigration and Inclusion); municipal building inspector
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the commercial premises (registered office, storage or fulfilment centre) do not constitute a listed activity under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act. Obtain a fire inspection certificate under the National Fire Code – Alberta Edition, verifying extinguishers, egress, and electrical compliance. Secure the building occupancy permit showing the authorized structural load capacity. Complete an OHS hazard assessment and workplace first-aid arrangement for any employees. Request a written EIA exemption determination from Alberta Environment and Protected Areas if a physical workspace is occupied, and retain that letter in the environmental compliance file.
required_dossiers: Fire inspection certificate / Fire Code compliance report
Building occupancy permit and structural load certificate
OHS hazard assessment and first-aid plan
EIA exemption determination request (if a physical workspace is occupied)
Waste handling policy covering e-waste, batteries, textiles and packaging (Alberta Recycling Regulation compliance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If deficiencies are cited, correct the non-compliant items, request re-inspection by the fire marshal or building inspector, and file a compliance plan or administrative appeal with the municipal safety codes office; for OHS orders, submit a written compliance plan within the statutory seven-day response window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal business licensing authority for the registered office municipality (e.g., City of Calgary Business Licensing under Business Licence Bylaw 6M96), with premises fire safety oversight by the local municipal fire marshal
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Second-Hand Goods Dealer Business Licence (applicable to online consignment and secondhand luxury goods resale operations)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no mandatory EIA Report or registration under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-3 for a non-industrial, low-footprint retail and storage use; a written exemption determination may be obtained for the corporate compliance record
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC point-source emissions. Sanitary sewage must connect to the municipal sewer system; e-waste, batteries, textile waste, and packaging must be disposed of in accordance with the Alberta Recycling Regulation (AR 91/2010) and applicable municipal waste bylaws; no hazardous substances may be stored at the premises beyond consumer-product quantities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire inspection certificate issued under the National Fire Code – Alberta Edition (fire alarm, extinguishers, and egress compliance); building occupancy permit with approved structural load rating; and Alberta OHS workplace hazard assessment, first-aid, and safety clearance covering all employees at the registered office and any storage or fulfilment premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - GST/HST portal: Business Registration Online (BRO), My Business Account, and GST/HST NETFILE; Alberta corporate income tax is administered by CRA on behalf of Alberta Finance under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity selling taxable supplies in Canada must obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) and a separate GST/HST account. Registration is made electronically through CRA's Business Registration Online (BRO) using Form RC1 (General Application) or Form RC460 (Non-Resident Corporation Application), supported by certified incorporation documents, registered alien address or Canadian agent, director/officer details, and the intended date of commercial activity. If the entity is not a small supplier, registration is mandatory before making taxable supplies. For an Alberta ULC, no separate provincial sales tax account is required because Alberta has no provincial sales tax; Alberta corporate tax registration is consolidated with the federal BN under the Alberta Corporate Income Tax Return (AT1).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Canadian check-the-box election exists; an unlimited liability corporation (ULC) is always a taxable Canadian corporation subject to entity-level federal and Alberta corporate income tax. For U.S. federal tax purposes, the ULC may be classified as a disregarded entity or partnership under IRC Section 7701/IRS Form 8832, but that foreign election has no effect on Canadian domestic taxation. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Income Tax Act (including CRA folio treatments under the OECD BEPS framework) may apply to Canadian-resident entities and cross-border hybrid instruments, but there is no elective regime for the ULC to opt into pass-through taxation in Canada.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax); Alberta is a non-participating province, so only the federal 5% GST applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in total worldwide taxable supplies made in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (small supplier threshold under Excise Tax Act Section 148). Non-resident vendors of digital/e-commerce services, including online resale platforms, must register for the simplified non-resident GST/HST regime once taxable Canadian supplies exceed CAD 30,000; a single platform or marketplace may be liable for collection on behalf of third-party sellers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory API-connected e-invoicing for GST/HST. Taxpayers may issue electronic invoices; the CRA requires full, supporting records in English or French, including sales, purchases, disbursement, and tax data. Large businesses may use EDI or XML-based e-invoicing voluntarily. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically via GST/HST NETFILE or through financial institution php services; no clearance from CRA is required before issuing an invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act if the goods are supplied by way of sale, possession passes, and the goods are delivered outside Canada by the vendor or the vendor's agent within specified time frames. Services are zero-rated if supplied to a non-resident person and not directly related to Canadian real property or Canadian tangible property, and the service is not performed in Canada for a non-resident who is present in Canada at the time. For online luxury consignment and secondhand goods, the vendor must prove physical exportation of the goods, maintain contracts with non-resident customers, and show safe delivery outside Canada. Digital services and performance obligations delivered electronically may qualify for zero-rating if the recipient is a non-resident and the service is not enjoyed in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Export Declaration via CBSA, forms B13A or Canada Border Services Agency electronic reporting)
Bill of Lading or air waybill showing foreign destination
Proof of payment / Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer record evidencing foreign currency settlement
Packing list and insurance documentation (where applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess a zero-rated export within a 4-year normal reassessment period, extendable to 10 years in cases of fraud, neglect, or misrepresentation. Penalties under the Excise Tax Act include: (i) failure to register penalties of up to 15% of the unremitted GST; (ii) false statements or omissions penalties of 10% of the tax paid or claimed, limited to the amount involved; (iii) gross negligence penalties up to 50% of the underestimated tax liability or overclaimed rebate; and (iv) interest at daily compounded prescribed rates on all unpaid GST/HST liabilities. Where CRA determines that claimed zero-rating was fraudulent or unsupported, the full GST at 5% is clawed back from the date of supply, plus interest and penalties, and criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act or Criminal Code may be pursued for deliberate falsification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), which operates a free-floating exchange-rate regime and administers no exchange-control licensing; prudential supervision of deposit-taking institutions is exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), and anti-money-laundering oversight of all cross-border payment and remittance activity is exercised by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility of the Canadian dollar (CAD) on both current-account and capital-account transactions. Neither the Currency Act, the Bank of Canada Act, nor the Income Tax Act imposes registration, licensing, or approval requirements for inward equity injections, dividend distributions, or repatriation of capital. Profit remittance encounters no exchange-control hurdle; the sole fiscal friction is Part XIII withholding tax of 25% on dividends paid to non-residents, potentially reduced to 5%-15% under an applicable bilateral income tax treaty (e.g., the Canada-United States convention), which is administered through bank documentation such as NR301 or W-8BEN-E forms rather than through FX administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Canada imposes no statutory repatriation timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation on export receipts. A Canadian entity may retain foreign-currency receivables indefinitely in domestic foreign-currency accounts or external bank accounts, and may freely elect the settlement currency. The only obligation is statistical: cross-border transactions above prescribed thresholds must be reported to Statistics Canada through the balance-of-payments survey routed via the entity's bank; this reporting is informational only and does not restrict timing, amount, or currency of settlement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account in dual-currency (CAD/USD) structure
Operational Account with integrated payment-feed solution
Capital Escrow Account and Trade Disbursement Account
Trade Settlement Account with commercial letter-of-credit desk
Operational Account with high-volume disbursement services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with material legal constraints. A foreign-regulated fintech EMI (e.g., Wise or Airwallex) may be used only as an auxiliary payment corridor, never as the primary treasury or escrow settlement account. Any EMI carrying on remittance, FX-dealing, or money-transfer business in Canada must separately hold a FINTRAC Money Service Business (MSB) registration and maintain a Canadian AML/ATF compliance program; provincial regimes (e.g., Ontario MSB licensing) may add further conditions. For a Medium-Risk-Enhanced luxury-resale entity, EMI throughput limits and source-of-funds freezes on high-ticket items are common, and foreign EMIs cannot deliver licensed escrow, commercial letters of credit, or CAD/USD clearing at Schedule I standards. Recommended structure: a Schedule I Canadian bank account as the treasury spine, with one FINTRAC-registered EMI used solely for low-value cross-border payouts and foreign-currency receivables collection, subject to the ULC's own due diligence on the EMI's FINTRAC/MSB status and sanctions compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid mandate: at least one director or ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) with signing authority must appear in person at a Canadian branch for identity verification and the account-opening interview; fully remote opening is not a standard option for Medium-Risk-Enhanced e-commerce corporates. Remote directors must provide notarized or bank-certified copies of valid photo identity and participate in a live audio-video call with the account officer. Under FINTRAC record-keeping rules, the bank must verify all directors, officers, and 25%+ UBOs of the Alberta ULC; the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Incorporation, an up-to-date extract from the Alberta Corporate Registry, and a Register of Individuals with Significant Control must accompany the application.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Second-hand luxury goods are categorized as high-risk for money laundering through over/under-invoicing, invoice discounting, and cash-equivalent settlement of consignment sales.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Item-level provenance and authentication package: original retail purchase receipts or third-party authentication certificates (Entrupy/GSI), signed consignment agreements, identity-and-address KYC data for each consignor, customs and export documentation for cross-border dispatches, and Escrow.com/Escrow Pay settlement statements demonstrating that funds flowed through a licensed escrow intermediary rather than peer-to-peer wallet transfers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Unlimited liability and tax-transparent pass-through attributes of the Alberta ULC may trigger enhanced governance review, particularly where multiple non-resident shareholders obscure beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of the ULC, the unanimous shareholders agreement, a current extract from the Alberta Corporate Registry identifying all UBOs, signed declarations of tax residence status, a duly completed Register of Individuals with Significant Control, and Canadian legal opinion confirming that the ULC is a valid separate legal person whose unlimited liability attaches only to shareholders, not to the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Sanctions and restricted-party exposure in a resale supply chain, where goods or counterparties may originate in, transit through, or settle to sanctioned jurisdictions or opaque online marketplaces.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Continuous sanctions-screening policy matched to the Canadian Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List and the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, an entity-level restricted-party ledger, an end-to-end payment-flow map showing settlement routed only from FINTRAC-registered processors and Schedule I banks, and a compliance attestation confirming that no transaction involves OFAC/UN-listed or enumerated jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Inability of the platform to evidence the legitimate source of wealth and funds behind high-ticket consignments, a predictor of third-party money laundering and purchase-with-stolen-funds exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-level audit trail from listing through authentication, storage, dispatch, and payout; consignor and buyer enhanced due-diligence files; historical chargeback and fraud-loss statistics from Stripe and Escrow Pay; and an annual independent AML/ATF audit report prepared under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, together with evidence of appointment of a registered compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections from non-resident shareholders settle by SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 COV for aggregated interbank transfers) into the ULC's Capital Escrow Account, with field 50K identifying the remitting shareholder and remittance information citing ISO 20022 category purpose code INTC (intercompany payment) together with the narrative 'inward equity capital contribution for common share subscription'. Canada imposes no exchange-control approval or pre-registration requirement. The bank will require (i) a directors' resolution authorizing the share issuance, (ii) the subscription or share-purchase agreement and an updated share register evidencing the funds as equity rather than shareholder debt, and (iii) a funds-received confirmation tagged under the Statistics Canada balance-of-payments classification for inward foreign direct investment (equity). To preserve the ULC's tax-transparent status, escrowed capital must remain segregated from operating cash; disbursement into the operational account is permitted only against documented trade payables and permitted operating expenses. On exit, capital repatriation and dividend distributions remit freely by SWIFT, subject to Part XIII withholding documentation and treaty relief forms.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements run primarily over SWIFT MT103 single-credit transfers and MT202 COV for high-value interbank payments, each carrying the underlying commercial invoice and contract reference in the remittance information fields. For high-ticket luxury inventory purchases, a Commercial Letter of Credit governed by UCP 600 (or an ISP 98 standby for performance) may be opened in favour of the supplier, payable against presentation of the commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or waybill, and an independent authentication report. Because CAD is freely convertible, settlement can occur in CAD, USD, EUR, or the supplier's chosen currency without FX approval. Marketplace payouts from Escrow Pay and Stripe clear through their partner Schedule I/II banks into the ULC operational account on a daily batch cycle; each payout transmits a transaction-level trace ID reconcilable to the platform ledger, preserving audit integrity for the banks and FINTRAC.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright CAD/USD and CAD/EUR foreign-exchange forward contracts with tenor up to 12-24 months, documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex
FX swaps and roll-over extensions for working-capital and trade-payment cycle management
Over-the-counter vanilla FX options (call and put structures) on USD/CAD and EUR/CAD exposures
Cross-currency swaps for matched asset-liability management where foreign-currency receivables are financed by foreign-currency debt

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs), permissible only where the counterpart currency is non-convertible (e.g., CNY, INR, KRW, BRL); NDFs are unnecessary for CAD itself because CAD is freely deliverable, and speculative open positions by an operating treasury are not permitted under Canadian bank credit policies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Form AR) — annual confirmation of registered office and directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each incorporation anniversary date (ABCA annual-return rule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No incremental late fee for a single year, but failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Registrar to administratively dissolve (strike off) the ULC; dissolution ends corporate existence and requires reinstatement application to Service Alberta. Directors who fail to comply may be liable for the offence provisions of the ABCA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (includes Alberta corporate tax under the federal-provincial Tax Collection Agreement; Schedule 50 corporate information attached)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end (e.g., Dec 31 year-end → file by June 30); balance-due day is 2 months after year-end for CCPC, 3 months for non-CCPC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under ITA 162(2): 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeated failure doubles the 5% base to 10%. Compound daily interest applies to unpaid instalments. Filing remains compulsory even where no tax is payable; prosecution/liability of officers may result.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST return (annual election using GST34 if gross revenue is C$400,000 or less; otherwise quarterly or monthly remittance filings)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filer: within 3 months after fiscal year-end; quarterly/monthly filers remit per their assigned CRA cycle. Alberta applies only 5% GST (no provincial component).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file: penalty of 5% of the unremitted balance plus 1% per month (maximum 12 months); balances carry compounded daily interest; directors of the ULC may be personally liable for unremitted GST under ETA section 323.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4 / T4A Statements of Remuneration Paid and T4 Summary (only if the ULC employs staff; otherwise N/A)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CRA — Payroll Deductions and Remittances (payroll account RC1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: T4 slips and T4 Summary filed on or before the last day of February following the calendar year; payroll remittances are made monthly/quarterly through the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquent T4 filing triggers a penalty of 3% of the unreported remuneration plus 1% per month (maximum 12 months), minimum C$100; second-year repeat failure raises the penalty to 10% plus 2% per month (maximum 20%). Director liability for unremitted payroll source deductions applies under ITA 227.1.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting (AGM) and audited financial statements, or unanimous written shareholder consents in lieu (ULC corporate-secretarial records)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book (maintained at registered office; not filed with a regulator unless subsequently attached to the T2 or produced upon demand)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM within 18 months of incorporation; thereafter each AGM must be held within 15 months of the prior AGM and at least once per calendar year (ABCA section 131)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM makes every involved director or officer guilty of an ABCA offence — maximum fine C$5,000 and/or 6 months' imprisonment; persistent non-compliance also blocks annual-return attestation and can contribute to administrative dissolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Auditor is mandatory at each AGM under ABCA section 208 unless the ULC meets the exemption: it is not a distributing corporation, has 15 or fewer shareholders, and all shareholders have unanimously resolved in any given year to waive the auditor. A private vintage-luxury ULC normally qualifies; failing the exemption, the audit can only be waived by an order of the court or by the Registrar in limited circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; private ULCs may elect ASPE (Canadian GAAP for private enterprises). Audited financial statements must present fairly per Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook; no SEC/US-GAAP-only presentation satisfies the statutory books requirement.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta-incorporated ULCs do not file an annual UBO return with a provincial registry. The Business Corporations Amendment Act, 2023 (Alberta) introduces maintenance of a register of individuals with significant control (ISC) at the corporation's records, with filing/registry phases being proclaimed. Each year, any share transfers are simultaneously endorsed in the Register of Transfers and the Register of Members, and the directors' slate is confirmed via the Alberta Annual Return; all registable information is verified at the AGM or by unanimous written consent.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors' Interests in Contracts
Minute Book (including unanimous shareholder consents and AGM minutes)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined general corporate tax rate in Alberta (15% federal Part I general rate plus 8% Alberta general corporate rate).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs) may access the small business deduction, reducing the combined federal-Alberta rate to 11% on active business income up to C$500,000 per associated group, subject to taxable capital limits. No sector-specific tax holiday applies to online consignment or secondhand luxury goods retail under ISIC 4791; Alberta ULCs are taxable corporations for Canadian income tax purposes and are not automatically flow-through entities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Canada CRA), filed electronically through CRA-approved EFILE/NetFile or CRA Corporation Internet Filing via My Business Account; Alberta corporate income tax is administered by the CRA under the provincial corporate tax collection agreement, so no separate Alberta corporate return is filed.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; installment payments are generally required quarterly during the taxation year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return must be filed within six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end. The balance of tax due is generally payable within two months after the fiscal year-end, with an extension to three months for certain CCPCs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Alberta jurisdiction of incorporation, ULC designation, CRA Business Number (BN), fiscal year-end date, registered office address, and Canadian residency status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada through a permanent establishment must obtain a non-resident BN and file T2; non-residents with only Canadian dividend or royalty income generally do not file T2 and instead file Part XIII returns/withholding forms.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 1, Line 100 - Gross Revenue and Net Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate gross revenue from online consignment commissions, resale margins, luxury inventory sales, escrow settlement fees, and any ancillary marketplace charges; deduct cost of goods sold, operating expenses, and allowance for bad debts to arrive at net income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source income allocable to a Canadian permanent establishment; e-commerce sales to Canadian customers without a Canadian PE are generally non-resident 'foreign business income' and excluded from T2 taxable income; clearly allocate Escrow and Stripe settlement flows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 5 - Province of Business / Alberta Allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apportionment of taxable income between provinces based on gross revenue attributable to permanent establishments and salaries/wages paid in Alberta; determines Alberta taxable income and provincial tax calculated at 8% general rate (or lower rate for qualifying CCPCs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents with a permanent establishment in more than one province or treaty country, complete the provincial allocation schedules using the CRA prescribed formula; Alberta taxes only the income allocated to Alberta activities and property.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 8 - Foreign Tax Credits and Cross-Border Issues
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim federal and Alberta foreign tax credits for taxes paid to other jurisdictions; disclose foreign-source income and foreign accrual property income (FAPI) involving controlled foreign affiliates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations generally cannot claim foreign tax credits except for Canadian-source income under an applicable tax treaty; ensure treaty-reduced rates are reported consistently with Part XIII withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form T106 - Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Comprehensive disclosure of related-party purchases/sales, consignment inventory advances, management fees, royalties, intercompany loans, and share transactions with non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory when the aggregate annual value of reportable transactions with each non-resident non-arm's-length party exceeds C$1,000,000; complete for all luxury inventory purchased or sold through related foreign platforms; failure to file can trigger transfer pricing penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under Income Tax Act (Canada) s.162: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month late up to 12 months; repeated failure within a three-year period increases to 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months. Non-filing corporations with no tax payable may face fixed penalties. Compound prescribed-rate interest accrues on unpaid taxes and penalties from the balance due date.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII Canadian withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, unless reduced by an applicable income tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain treaty-reduced withholding, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide the paying Alberta ULC with a valid U.S. IRS Form W-8BEN-E or W-8BEN, or CRA Form NR301, completed before payment. The ULC must reasonably know the treaty entitlement; CRA may require a Certificate of Residency from the treaty jurisdiction (e.g., IRS Form 6166) and supporting beneficial ownership evidence. If excess tax was withheld, the non-resident may file CRA Form NR7 for a refund within the applicable limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 25% Part XIII withholding on interest and royalty payments to non-residents. Under the Canada-U.S. Income Tax Convention, arm's-length interest generally qualifies for 0% withholding, and royalty payments for patents, trademarks, know-how and similar property generally qualify for 10% withholding, with certain copyright royalties eligible for 0%; non-treaty jurisdictions remain subject to the 25% statutory rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Form T106 is mandatory where reportable non-arm's-length cross-border transactions with a single non-resident exceed C$1,000,000 in a taxation year; a Country-by-Country Report is mandatory for multinational groups with consolidated revenue of C$750,000,000 or more. Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation must be prepared and retained by the Alberta ULC for all material controlled transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Alberta has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations, but Canadian courts and CRA will disregard artificial corporate structures under the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) in Income Tax Act s.245, the sham doctrine, and treaty abuse rules under the OECD Multilateral Instrument. Real economic substance must include active board decisions in Canada, salaried employees, inventory management, contract negotiation, and consignment platform operations; a ULC with minimal employees or assets is vulnerable to recharacterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understatement or omission of online consignment and resale revenue; routing Stripe or Escrow settlements to offshore accounts; creating fictitious supplier invoices for 'vintage' inventory; false or incomplete T2 filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Gross negligence penalty under ITA s.163(2) of 50% of the understated tax; criminal tax evasion under ITA s.239 punishable by a fine equal to 50%-200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to five years; CRA may reassess without a normal limitation period where misrepresentation is fraudulent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who authorize or participate in evasion are personally liable for criminal fines and imprisonment; CRA can assert director liability under s.227.1 for unremitted source deductions; courts may impose asset freezes, restitution orders, and travel restrictions pending criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing vintage luxury resale inventory or platform services with a related foreign company at non-arm's-length markups; paying excessive management or royalty fees to a low-tax affiliate; omitting Form T106.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ITA s.247(2) allows CRA to adjust taxable income to arm's-length amounts; ITA s.247(3) imposes a penalty of 10% of the net transfer pricing adjustment where contemporaneous documentation is inadequate or transactions are not arm's length; statutory interest accrues on reassessed tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve false documentation or incomplete T106 filings may be subject to ITA s.163.2 penalties for participation in a false statement; their personal assets can be used to satisfy judgments where they are privy to deliberate gross negligence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming an Alberta ULC with no office, employees, banking activity, or real decision-making solely to convert Canadian e-commerce income into tax-free shareholder loans or treaty-exempt dividends; interposing an unlimited liability company for offshore loss absorption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR under ITA s.245 permits CRA to deny the tax benefit, recharacterize transactions, and reassess; if the arrangement involves a tax treaty benefit, the Principal Purpose Test under the Multilateral Instrument may remove treaty access; CRA penalties and interest attach to the re-determined income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: In a ULC, shareholders have unlimited liability for the corporation's debts; directors can be personally assessed for unpaid corporate tax withholdings and for knowingly signing returns based on sham documentation; civil fraudulent conveyance actions may pierce any remaining protections.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Escrow or Stripe payment forwarding to conceal the origin or destination of high-value luxury resale proceeds; accepting third-party payments without identifying sellers/buyers; structuring transactions to avoid reporting; failing to maintain FINTRAC records for large virtual currency transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to comply with Canada's Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Financing Act can result in administrative monetary penalties; money laundering under the Criminal Code is indictable with imprisonment up to ten years; CRA and FINTRAC can freeze accounts and seize assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly direct or permit evasive AML practices are exposed to criminal prosecution, personal fines, imprisonment, and court-ordered restitution; departure bans and asset freezes may be imposed pending criminal proceedings.
